title: admission-probe-metrics-and-rollback-register
body:
Purpose and scope

This note captures a compact, operational-first approach for admitting speculative-decoding-enabled model variants into the serving fleet. It focuses on small, repeatable experiments (admission probes), the metric catalog we should use to accept/reject a variant, and an operator-friendly rollback register and automated triggers. This is intentionally pragmatic — a checklist + guardrail doc meant to be usable by on-call and release engineers during model rollouts.

Background / motivation

We often need to deploy model variants (quantized, alternative kernels, or smaller decoders) that make non-trivial tradeoffs: lower cost at potential accuracy/latency regressions, or different kernel paths that change memory pressure on KV caches. Past rollouts have shown two common failures: (1) slow observable regressions that only appear after cache warming, and (2) transient kernel stalls under high scheduling contention. The admission-probe concept below is designed to catch both early.

Key concepts (new-ish terms used here)

- Admission probe: a lightweight, traffic-limited copy of production traffic routed to the candidate variant to exercise kernels, scheduling, and KV behaviour without full customer exposure.
- Headstart window: a short period (configurable minutes) where probes run with slightly relaxed latency SLOs to allow KV warmup and kernel JIT paths to hit steady state.
- Echo metric: a synthetic signal injected into the probe path that can be used to detect kernel-level determinism/regression (see "signal tokens" below).
- Confidence-stacked rollback: multi-level automatic rollback where increasingly aggressive actions are taken as metric deviations grow.

Admission probe design

1) Traffic selection
- Use a small sample (0.5–2%) of production requests for live probes. Prefer long-tail requests and requests with representative sequence lengths (short/med/long buckets) so KV cache effects surface.
- For heavy stateful sessions (chat), prefer sampling at session start rather than mid-conversation to avoid inconsistent experience.

2) Probe routing and isolation
- Route probes to a separate pool (probe pool) with identical infra configuration but isolated quotas and metrics.
- Probe pool must have explicit per-node KV namespaces to avoid thrashing global cache. KV warmup can be simulated via synthetic prefixes (see "synthetic warmup" below).

3) Headstart window
- Default headstart: 15 minutes. During headstart: relax latency SLO by +25% and allow up to +10% token-cost variance. These tolerances let quantized kernels and JITs reach steady-state without immediate rollback noise.
- After headstart, enforce normal SLOs and escalate metrics assessment.

4) Echo/instrumentation tokens
- Inject a small percentage (1–2%) of requests with a hidden probe prefix that triggers additional verification traces in kernel stacks (non-customer-visible). These tokens allow us to compare internal activations and determinism for kernel variants versus baseline.
- Echo checks produce lightweight diffs (hashes) that are aggregated: echo_match_rate should be near 100% for deterministic kernels; divergence >0.5% needs human review.

Metric catalog (what we measure, why, and thresholds)

A) correctness / quality
- production-llr-delta (approx): produced via offline evals and sampled customers. Threshold: < 1.5% change in chosen eval metric (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR surrogate) for admission.
- echo_match_rate: probe-only. Threshold: > 99.5% after headstart.

B) latency and tail behaviour
- p50_latency_delta and p95_latency_delta (candidate vs baseline): threshold p95_delta < +10% after headstart.
- kernel_hang_count: number of kernel stalls detected by watchdogs (>500ms no-progress). Threshold: 0 for admission; any non-zero triggers immediate investigation.

C) KV cache health
- kv_hit_rate_probe: target >= baseline - 5% after 30m.
- kv_eviction_rate: see acceptable window: < 0.1 evictions/sec/node sustained. Spikes on deployment can be tolerated if headstart-active and drop < 60 minutes.
- kv_warmup_time: time to reach 90% steady-state hit rate; target < 20 minutes for admission.

D) scheduling and resource pressure
- scheduler_wait_ratio: % time requests spend queued vs executing. Threshold: < baseline + 5%.
- gpu_mem_spill_events: any event must be documented; repeated spills cause rollback.

E) safety / error signals
- decode_error_rate: threshold < baseline + 0.1% absolute.
- token_conflict_rate: rate of inconsistent token outputs in mirrored requests; threshold <= 0.05%.

Composite acceptance rule (automatic gate)
- After headstart, admission = true only if:
  * echo_match_rate >= 99.5% AND
  * p95_latency_delta < +10% AND
  * production-llr-delta < 1.5% AND
  * kv_hit_rate_probe >= baseline - 5% AND
  * kernel_hang_count == 0
- If any single metric breaches a severe threshold (kernel_hang_count > 0, gpu_mem_spill_events > 0), immediate rollback (see rollback policy).

Rollback register and actions (confidence-stacked rollback)

Level 0 — soft rollback (automated, non-disruptive)
- Action: stop new probe traffic (set probe traffic to 0%), keep existing probe pool running for diagnostics.
- Trigger: minor metric breach during headstart (e.g., p95_delta between +10–20% but no hangs).
- Operator note: preserves artifacts for post-mortem and allows quick re-enable.

Level 1 — revert rollout (automated, conservative)
- Action: switch serving config for candidate variant back to baseline for new sessions; gracefully drain active probe sessions (drain policy: allow up to 60s or until completion).
- Trigger: quality regressions > 1.5% OR any kernel_hang_count > 0.

Level 2 — safety rollback (manual ack required if auto-disabled)
- Action: evict candidate variant from cluster, evict KV namespace associated, run KV integrity check, and invalidate caches for nodes where inconsistent behavior seen.
- Trigger: repeated gpu_mem_spill_events or token_conflict_rate > 0.5%. Requires incident lead to ack.

Operational runbook (quick checklist for on-call)

1) Alert fires (e.g., kernel_hang_count > 0):
  - Immediately set probe_traffic_pct -> 0.
  - Tag all metrics with probe-run id and collect full diagnostic bundle (traces, kernel logs, KV telemetry).
  - Open incident in Slack #serving-ops and assign an engineer.

2) If p95 latency regresses:
  - Check headstart window: if still in headstart, wait until headstart end unless kernel_hang_count is non-zero.
  - If post-headstart, initiate Level 1 rollback.

3) If KV eviction storm observed:
  - Lower probe pool concurrency, reduce batch sizes on probe pool, and run synthetic warmup for baseline to compare.
  - If evictions persist > 30 minutes, escalate to Level 2.

Synthetic warmup and deterministic comparators

- Synthetic warmup: a controlled series of artificial requests primed with representative prefixes to warm KV cache across probe nodes before opening to live probe traffic. Warmup should be used for variants that change model context size or quantization layout.
- Deterministic comparators: run a small corpus of fixed, canonical prompts through baseline and candidate off the critical path. Compare output hashes and token-level timing traces to detect micro-regressions. Store comparator runs in S3 under test-run ids for audit.

Chaos and fault-injection experiments (pre-admit tests)

Before admission to production probes, run nightly chaos experiments in a staging cluster:
- induce kernel schedule preemption (simulate background noise threads), check kernel_hang_count reaction.
- force KV eviction pressure (artificial dataset size) and measure kv_hit_rate and kv_eviction_rate.
- disable one GPU mid-request on a subset of nodes to test graceful fallbacks and monitor request rewrites.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- Sampling strategy: session-start vs uniform sampling; session-start reduces user-facing surface but may miss mid-session regressions.
- Headstart leniency: how long before tolerance becomes a masking risk? Current default 15 minutes is a compromise.
- Automatic rollback aggressiveness: do we allow Level-1 auto-reverts for non-critical customers (e.g., internal only) while requiring manual for public traffic?

Action items (next steps)

- (Maya) Draft PR that wires these metrics into the rollout controller (github PR referenced above).
- (Oliver) Implement echo_token injection with hash aggregation; add to probe pool instrumentation.
- (Samir) Add kv_warmup synthetic routine and a staging job to run warmup before any probe starts.
- (Ava/Diego) Run 3 staged chaos experiments against the nightly variant build and report: kernel hang injection, KV eviction stress, and GPU preemption.

Appendix: handy command snippets

- Disable probe traffic quickly: rctl set-probe-traffic --pool probe-<id> --pct 0
- Collect probe bundle: telemetry collect --scope probe-<id> --out /tmp/probe-bundle-<id>.tgz
- Re-enable after soft rollback: rctl set-probe-traffic --pool probe-<id> --pct <previous-pct> (only after green signal)

Notes to reviewers

This doc is intentionally prescriptive and operational. It should be merged with the rollout-controller RFC once we've iterated on the numeric thresholds with real probe runs. Feedback wanted especially on: the headstart defaults, echo token design (privacy considerations), and kv_warmup time targets.

-- end --
